summary:
I adopted V1's fix4 for the seam beside a slanted hidden gap, and the gate holds. Edge.hiddenGap now asks the part across first, then any part of the set except the face's own part, for each face's probe. Each crossing point must also lie within REACH (HIDE_OFFSET + 2·EPS_GEOM) of the other point, measured across along its face's normal.

Two changes from fix4:
- I dropped fix4's reach pre-tests. A probe held within EPS_GEOM already implies them, so they decided nothing, and fix4 never charged its loop's box tests.
- The gap-across test runs first. Every normal, box test and sd is now charged, so a far chord costs one normal.

**The set: each caller's own.** Thinness asks its work set W, which on All is every kept part (the measure's own hiders). The raster asks the striking slot's kept parts. Using every kept part instead moved the edge of 7 fixtures, 13 ribbed bars' edges and 2 ribbed bars' Sharpening Thinness, with no d. Every one of the joins it added (10 on fixtures, 48 on ribbed bars) runs the line through a guard, grip or pommel part, so it counted that part's metal into the blade's thickness. A part of another slot only *beside* a gap reads the gap open (V1's laminate with the seam piece labelled Guard: edge mean thickness −4.5 %); its label is visible (O8).

**Results.**
- V1's seam cases now read as the same pieces 0.0100 apart, within 0.0006: 0.3095 Hard → 0.1734, 0.2104 Hard → 0.1343.
- Fixer D's 0–75° sweep, his non-facing neighbours, 1,152,000 two-part lines and the P3 channel are all unchanged; nothing the verdict shows merges.
- No fixture, generated design, golden or digest moved. On the plausible set, 10 ribbed bars move d by ≤ 0.0173 (V1's 10), with no tier change.
- Gate: worst valid 8 projects to 53.6–54.3 ms (the largest ratio of any design gives 56.0), against 57.
- Attack designs built to stress the loop take 19–30 ms, with longest stretches of 0.21–0.28 ms. Every query is charged; a call costs at most 94 units.

**Tests.** I folded V1's five tried tests and V2's three-plate case into Edge.spec, Factors.spec and Invariance.spec. All 30 mutants are killed by `--quick`. Under the set rule, EH13–15 and m_edgelast become equivalent on parallel plates, so I added three non-parallel run cases that kill them. The new tests that target the round's fix fail on m3-r3-base; the rest pass there and kill their mutants.

**Text.** Updated §4.6 row 1, §5.2, a clause in §5.5, §5.6, §14.6 T-DIF-04 and T-EDG-01, the Edge and Factors headers, E-S2.13, and my M3-notes section. Nothing was re-blessed because no value moved.

**Verify:** exit 1, 743 pass and 1 fail. Only T-PERF-01's timing failed (worst valid 5 at 62.14 ms), with the machine 26–61 % busy. Nothing committed; docs.rar untouched.

My text only mentions the mouth as the reason for the three/four-plate test's 0.01 tolerance (0.0073 and 0.0075 at 0.0119). The 45° seam residue (26 of 49 Hard) rides on that drift plus O11.

For the lead, the set: a gap whose only hider is a part of another slot beside it reads open in the raster and in Sharpening's set. On V1's 30° laminate with the seam piece labelled Guard, the edge's mean thickness is −4.5 % at 0.0105 while Hammering holds. I treated it as a visible label (O8).

For the lead: 40 hidden-gap joins on 4 plausible ribbed bars cross air that is not within MERGE_GAP of two parts at all 9 points checked. These are Z lines grazing a rod 0.0003–0.001 off its surface between two staves the rod hides. No value moves, and a line 0.001 lower merges the same span plainly.

Theoretical worst case per Thinness probe: at most 4 chords × 48 calls × 94 units. It is charged with the probe, but in one report. No constructed design came near it (largest call 39 units, longest stretch 0.28 ms). If one ever does, charging inside unionChord would split it.

T-PERF-01 has not run on a quiet machine on this tree. It failed in verify (worst valid 5, 62.14 ms, 26–61 % busy) and alone (F2 stretch 0.404 ms, 25–62 % busy). The lead's quiet verify and S-PAR-02 run are still needed before the commit; the digest did not move this round.
